name: Nongkhnum River Island
description: Largest river island in Meghalaya and one of the larger ones in Asia, formed by the bifurcation of the Kynshi River into Phanliang and Namliang rivers near Nongstoin. Features sandy beaches, clear river channels, grasslands, and nearby waterfalls; offers picnics, camping, and peaceful nature walks in a relatively unspoiled setting.
facts: About 14-18 km from Nongstoin, West Khasi Hills HQ
Accessed via bridge or ferry over Kynshi; permits may be needed

name: Langshiang Falls
description: One of the tallest waterfalls in Meghalaya, plunging approximately 337 metres from the Kynshi River into a deep gorge near Sangriang village. Surrounded by forests and rolling hills; best viewed from Mawpon village or after a short trek. A dramatic offbeat natural wonder.

name: Weinia Falls (Kshaid Weinia)
description: Powerful waterfall on the Kynshi River near Nongkhnum Island, cascading amid dense forests and cliffs. Popular for its scenic power, especially in monsoon; short walk from parking on Nongkhnum Road. Combines well with visits to the river island.
facts: Address often listed as Nongkhnum Road, 793119

name: Nongstoin Town
description: Headquarters of West Khasi Hills district, a hill town at about 1,400 m elevation serving as the main base for exploring the district's river islands, waterfalls, and Khasi cultural sites. Features local markets, administrative offices, and access via NH to Shillong.
facts: District HQ of West Khasi Hills

name: Pamphyrnai Lake
description: Serene natural lake about 10 km from Nongstoin, nestled among hillocks with clear waters and surrounding greenery. Developed as a local picnic and recreation spot; offers quiet walks, fishing, and photography away from major tourist circuits.
facts: Approximately 10 km from Nongstoin near Ksehkohlong
Managed locally; popular with nearby residents

name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, a colonial-era hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known for its cool climate, pine forests, educational institutions, markets, and as the main base for exploring the Khasi Hills.
facts: HQ of East Khasi Hills district

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at approximately 1,961 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and on clear days the plains of Bangladesh. Sacred to the Khasi people with a small shrine; access involves ID check near an Air Force station.

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall (locally Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew) on the outskirts of Shillong, set amid fern-covered rocks and lush greenery. Easily accessible with stairs leading to viewing points at different levels.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center
Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, near Sohra (Cherrapunji), plunging into a green plunge pool. Fed by plateau rainfall; dramatic especially in monsoon. Associated with a local Khasi legend of Ka Likai.
facts: One of the most iconic falls in Meghalaya

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town on the southern Khasi Hills plateau, formerly known as Cherrapunji, famous for extremely high rainfall, spectacular waterfalls, living root bridges, limestone caves, and viewpoints over the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Sub-divisional town in East Khasi Hills
Base for Nohkalikai, Mawsmai, and root bridge treks

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Small Khasi village near the Bangladesh border renowned as one of the cleanest villages in Asia (Discover India award 2003). Features living root bridges, bamboo walkways, orchid gardens, and community-led eco-tourism in a matrilineal society.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-level living root bridge (Jingkieng Nongriat) woven from Ficus elastica aerial roots by Khasi villagers over generations in Nongriat village. Requires a steep trek of ~3,500 steps from Tyrna; one of the most famous bioengineered structures in the world.
facts: In Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills
Lower bridge estimated over 180 years old
Best in dry season; closed Sundays sometimes

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit village, featuring steep green ridges, deep valleys, and expansive sky views. A popular day-trip from Shillong for photography and short walks along the rim.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village, protected by Khasi tradition for centuries. Dense primary forest with old trees, moss, orchids, and biodiversity; entry often with local guide and rules against removing anything.
facts: No extraction of plants or materials allowed

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave (Krem Mawsmai) near Sohra with stalactites, stalagmites, and fossil-like formations. Short, lit passages suitable for casual visitors; name means 'oath stone' in Khasi.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall plunging about 315 m from limestone cliffs near Mawsmai village, visible mainly in the rainy season. Dramatic panoramic views of the cascade and distant plains.

name: Don Bosco Museum (Centre for Indigenous Cultures)
description: Seven-floor museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artefacts, lifestyles, and traditions of Northeast India's indigenous peoples. Extensive ethnographic collection including costumes, tools, and housing models.

name: Ward's Lake (Pollock Lake)
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, built in 1894, surrounded by botanical gardens, cobblestone paths, a wooden bridge, and boating facilities. A popular urban recreational and picnic spot.
facts: Also known as Pollock Lake or Nan Polok
